title: Packrat ask collage and remediation lab — customer ask synthesis
body:
Purpose and framing:
This is a packrat-style collage of recent customer asks (Apr–Nov 2026) that felt adjacently fixable with low engineering lift. Goal: surface a short list of small, decoupled remediations we can prototype in 1–3 sprints to reduce noise, unblock customers, and create quick wins for Dedicated/Hosted users. Not exhaustive — intentionally messy (notes-to-self style).

Note on method:
- Source mix: CSM notes, support threads, field interviews, partner calls, and two post-mortems (latency incidents).
- Quick triage: flagged as "fast patch" if estimated dev < 5d and rollback-safe.
- Where useful I attach a heuristic for impact (qualitative) and a risk grade.

Representative customer synopses (verbatim-ish):
- "We keep getting large context blowups when users paste transcripts — tokens spike and latency tanks." — mid-market search-ops lead.
- "When the model falls back to the smaller variant, embeddings permissions get buggy for our indexer." — startup CTO.
- "Tool-calls return with truncated arrays; sometimes functions timeout but the UI still shows success." — enterprise platform team.

Observed themes (short):
- token spikes / long input handling (prefix trimming edgecases)
- inconsistent fallback semantics across deployments (hosted vs dedicated)
- KV cache warm/cold behavior causing 2–3x latency variance at session start
- tooling/observability edges: token-level billing mismatches reported by customers
- function/tool calling truncation + silent success states

Packrat remediation proposals (quick hits):
1) Prefix-safe trim utility (server-side opt-in flag)
   - Symptom: huge user paste triggers long seqs, OOMs, and high tail latency.
   - Quick fix: server middleware to detect >X tokens and automatically compress (strip filler, truncate from head with heuristic), returning a warning metadata flag to client.
   - Est dev: 3d (1d spec + 2d implement test).
   - Impact: high for chat-heavy customers.
   - Risk: low (opt-in, reversible).
   - Linked: JIRA-3381 (customer replication cases)

2) Fallback semantics checklist and regression test (canonical matrix)
   - Symptom: behavior differs when routing between hosted/dedicated/private — causes permission and embedding indexer failures.
   - Quick fix: create a small test harness + checklist to verify call semantics (auth, headers, model variant metadata) and add to nightly smoke.
   - Est dev: 4d (test harness + 2 automated checks).
   - Impact: medium/high (reduces deploy regressions).
   - Risk: low

3) KV cache warmups + cold-start signal (client-visible header)
   - Symptom: 2–3x latency variance on first gen after session start; customers interpret as instability.
   - Quick fix: expose a boolean header "x-rw-cache-ready" or similar and emit warmup traces; add documentation snippet and SDK helper that pre-warms common prefixes.
   - Est dev: 5d for server + SDK helper.
   - Impact: medium
   - Risk: low/medium (surface-only changes).

4) Function-call sanity wrapper (truncate arrays + explicit error state)
   - Symptom: tool outputs truncated arrays and UI shows inconsistent success.
   - Quick fix: add a server-side validation pass: if function output expected schema but missing elements, return structured error with code and include full raw output in debug log.
   - Est dev: 3d
   - Impact: medium (enterprise automation users).
   - Risk: low (non-breaking, adds explicit error path).

5) Token-billing reconciliation helper (ops-side)
   - Symptom: customers reporting token billing divergence between console and their tracking.
   - Quick fix: exportable reconciler CSV that maps request-id -> model -> token-count -> client-reported-token-count; shipping as a console button for accounts with billing disputes.
   - Est dev: 4d (backend export + small UI).
   - Impact: low/medium but high trust.
   - Risk: low

Quick prioritization matrix (for stakeholder pick):
- Low effort / high impact: Prefix-safe trim utility, Function-call sanity wrapper.
- Low effort / medium impact: Fallback semantics checklist.
- Slightly larger: KV cache warmups (small SDK + server work).
- Trust play: Token-billing reconciler.

Open questions / investigations to run:
- What threshold for automatic prefix trim is acceptable? Quick A/B candidate: 20k tokens vs 50k. Need samples from top 5 customers.
- Can fallback matrix be turned into an automated governance rule (block rollouts that don't match the matrix)?
- Will the cache-ready header reveal internal routing that security teams object to in private deployments? Check with privacy/compliance.

Next steps (actionable, 1–2 week horizon):
- PM sync: Elena and Marcus to scope Prefix-safe trim (spec + sample inputs) by Nov 29.
- Eng spike: Anika to prototype function-call validation on staging; deliver RFC + demo by Dec 3.
- Ops: Request billing export sample generation for 3 disputed accounts (Riley to open JIRA ticket).

Loose notes / rambling bits for later:
- "Packrat" approach useful: keep one living doc for small fixes; if >3 sprints, promote to product roadmap.
- Consider naming these "runtime microfixes" and create a dedicated backlog label.
- Slack thread: #runtime-vouchers has 6 messages referencing truncated functions — collect and attach specific message ids.

Quick wins checklist (for the release lead):
- [ ] Add opt-in prefix-trim flag to model config UI
- [ ] Create regression harness ticket (fallback matrix)
- [ ] Add SDK helper to call pre-warm with common prefixes
- [ ] Surface structured function-call errors in console logs
- [ ] Add "export token reconciliation" button behind account admin role

Attachments / references:
- Repro snippets (pasted in JIRA-3381)
- Confluence: runtime/packrat-microfix-playbook (draft)
- Slack: runtime-vouchers thread (requested message ids will be appended)

Notes-to-self: keep this intentionally rough. If we get consensus on the two quick wins (prefix-trim + function-call wrapper) start a 2-sprint fastlane and loop in solutions-engineering for customer pilot.
